links.outcome: Error detection sensitivity and review time of GPT-4 versus human radiologist readers on same reports
links.effect: Human readers had worse factual error detection sensitivity (0.33-0.69 vs 0.89) and took longer (82-121 s vs 16 s, P<.001) than GPT-4.
links.quote: Compared with GPT-4, human readers had worse factual error detection sensitivity (0.33-0.69 vs 0.89; P = .008 for radiologist 4, P < .001 for others) and took longer to review (82-121 seconds vs 16 seconds, P < .001).

unlisted_practices: Using an LLM as a proofreading tool to detect and revise errors in radiology reports
Optimizing LLM prompts on a development subset before evaluation

screen.reason: Evaluates the feasibility and performance of GPT-4 as an automated proofreading tool for radiology reports compared to human readers, without testing a specific operational guardrail or deployment practice.
